title: The Pond
text:
Welcome to The Pond, an interactive learning environment to learn how to make your science more open and reproducible.
Whether you are new to open science or looking to deepen your technical skills, The Pond is designed to let you learn by doing.

title: The Pond
text:
Explore The Pond




The Shallows
Start here to explore why open science matters. Learn about the ideas behind open, reproducible, and FAIR science and the problems these practices are designed to solve.

Enter The Shallows







LilyPads
Hop onto a LilyPad for hands-on learning. Explore self-contained modules, courses, and project workstations focused on data, software, and scientific workflows.

Explore the LilyPads







The Deep End
Ready to dive deeper? Explore advanced topics and technical tracks, including licensing frameworks, infrastructure, and more complex approaches to implementing open science.

Dive into The Deep End







The Spring
Open science is a community effort. Ask questions, share experiences, and continue the conversation with other learners and practitioners.

Visit The Spring

title: The Pond
text:
Where should I start?
New to open science? Begin in The Shallows.
Looking for practical skills? Jump straight to the LilyPads.
Already comfortable with the basics? Dive into The Deep End.

title: LilyPads
text:
LilyPads are hands-on learning spaces where you can build practical skills for making your research more open and reproducible.
Choose a place to land.




Data
Learn how to find, organize, document, clean, share, and preserve research data so that others — including your future self — can understand and reuse it.

Explore Data







Software
Learn practices for creating reusable and sustainable research software, from version control and documentation to testing, licensing, and publishing.

Explore Software







Workflow
Learn how to make the entire path from data to results reproducible, including computational environments, provenance, notebooks, and sharing complete workflows.

Explore Workflows

title: Workflow
text:
These LilyPads build on one another. Start with LilyPad 1 and work through them in order.




1. Are Methods Actionable?
Try to reproduce a scientific result from a methods description—and discover what information is missing.
Start LilyPad →






2. What Is a Workflow?
Explore what scientists mean by a workflow and identify the pieces needed to make one reproducible.
Start LilyPad →






3. Sketching a Workflow
Turn a scientific process into a visual workflow by identifying its major steps and connections.
Start LilyPad →






4. From Sketch to Notebook
Connect the steps in a workflow sketch to the code, data, and outputs in a computational notebook.
Start LilyPad →






5. Why Containers Matter
See how changing the computational environment can change scientific results—even when the workflow stays the same.
Start LilyPad →






6. Citing Workflows
Explore how computational workflows can be documented, shared, and cited as research products.
Start LilyPad →

title: Are Methods Actionable?
text:
NoteInstructions



Chances are you have come across results in scientific publications, posters or talks, and wondered: “How did they get here?” Supposedly that is what the Methods section explains, but that information is not always actionable.
The paragraph below is an excerpt from a (fictitious) methods section. The goal of the exercise is to determine whether the provided instructions are sufficient to reproduce the results shown in Figure 1. As you complete this exercise, take careful notes about what information is missing from the methods section that would help you reproduce the results.


We examined interannual variability in the El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) using spectral analysis. Results of this analysis are shown in Figure 1.



Figure 1. Spectral power of ENSO variability.
